polls.description: Major AI companies are scrambling to secure power infrastructure as data centers strain energy grids and face public backlash over resource consumption.
polls.question: Should AI companies be allowed to bypass public grids with private generators?

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic buys $3.4bn of gas generators for its data centres, FT reports
cluster_stories.summary: Anthropic has agreed to pay $3.4bn for gas-fired generators to power its data centres, the Financial Times reported on Sunday. The FT said it is the biggest known single buy of power kit by an AI company. The deal covers 1.7 gigawatts of large generators, the FT said, citing one person who knows about it. The letter from chief executive Michael Intrator was sent on Saturday, Bloomberg reported. Intrator offered to work with her transition team on finishing projects that already have permits. cluster_stories.title: Can’t cook or shower: Indonesians take aim at data centers
cluster_stories.summary: Frustration is bubbling over in Indonesia and Malaysia — especially in regions bordering Singapore that are seen as a prime location for new tech facilities.
cluster_stories.headline: Data Centers Strain Power Grids in Indonesia and Malaysia

cluster_stories.title: Voters Put the AI Data Center Boom on Notice
cluster_stories.summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News tech reporter Brody Ford explains how voter backlash against data centers could disrupt the rapid buildout of infrastructure powering the AI boom. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ford discusses the risks for heavily indebted AI companies and whether tougher promises from newly elected officials will translate into meaningful restrictions on development. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: Voter Backlash Threatens AI Data Center Boom

polls.description: Growing concerns about AI risks are driving new regulatory efforts, ethics research, and security measures from government and researchers.
polls.question: Should governments prioritize AI safety regulation or innovation freedom?

cluster_stories.title: US Justice Department sets up an AI task force under its new SI name
cluster_stories.summary: The US Justice Department has set up a task force to lead its work on AI crimes and AI lawsuits. It is called the Super Intelligence Task Force, the department said on Thursday. The name follows a September order from President Donald Trump telling federal agencies to call AI “super intelligence” in official documents. cluster_stories.headline: DOJ Launches Super Intelligence Task Force for AI Crimes
